subject: humanities
passage: Bossa nova, which emerged in Rio de Janeiro in the late 1950s, grew out of samba, the lively dance music of Brazil's carnival. Yet the new style sounded strikingly different. Musicians such as the guitarist and singer João Gilberto reduced samba's crowd of drums to a gentle rhythm played on a single guitar, and they borrowed the rich, complex chords of American cool jazz. Singers, rather than projecting over a band, sang softly, almost as if speaking to one listener. The result was an intimate music that soon found eager audiences far beyond Brazil.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Bossa nova replaced samba as the main music of Brazil's carnival.
choices.B: João Gilberto was the first musician in Brazil to play American jazz chords.
choices.C: Bossa nova singers sang softly instead of projecting over a band.
choices.D: Bossa nova turned elements of samba into a quieter, more intimate music.

explanation.why: The text says bossa nova "grew out of samba" but "sounded strikingly different," then lists the changes: a gentle guitar rhythm, jazz chords, and soft singing. It concludes that the result was "an intimate music." The main idea must cover both its roots in samba and its transformation.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text never says bossa nova replaced samba at carnival.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text says musicians borrowed jazz chords but never claims Gilberto was the first in Brazil to do so.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Soft singing is only one of several changes the text describes.
explanation.D: Correct. This covers the whole text: bossa nova came from samba but changed it into a quiet, intimate style.
